head.title: It finds passwords in text, and crosses them out.
head.lede: That is the whole thing. Everything below is about doing it carefully.

atTheBoundary.title: Text in, the same text out
lede: : from your credential manager, through a vault, to the provider. Redact Secret is a filter you install on every other road. Text goes in, the same text comes out, minus anything that looked like a credential.

beingHonest.title: What it is not
beingHonest.limitsTitle: Pick a repository scanner instead if you need these
items: credential families against Gitleaks' several hundred rules. Precision was chosen over recall, deliberately.
It never asks a provider whether a key is live, so it cannot tell you a match is definitely real.
No commit archaeology, no repository crawling, no baseline files.
There is no policy console, no quarantine and no hosted service.
The personal-data families are off by default and every one of them is
— availability is not a support claim.

rule.b: Browser scanning is a courtesy; server scanning is the actual boundary.
